{{Short description|none}}
[[Image:WorldPopulation.png|thumb|right|350px|Graph showing population by continent as a percentage of [[world population]] (1750–2005)]]
[[File:Population density map of the world.svg|right|thumb|350px|Map of [[List of countries and dependencies by population density|countries by population density]]]]
The continent of [[Asia]] covers 29.4% of the Earth's land area and has a population of around 4.87 billion ({{as of|2022|lc=y}}),<ref name="UN Population Division">{{cite web |title=Asia Population |url=https://population.un.org/wpp/Graphs/Probabilistic/POP/TOT/935 |website=World Population Prospects 2022 |publisher=United Nations |access-date=23 January 2023 |archive-date=23 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230123200523/https://population.un.org/wpp/Graphs/Probabilistic/POP/TOT/935 |url-status=dead }}</ref> accounting for about 60% of the world population. The combined population of both [[China]] and [[India]] is estimated to be over 2.8 billion people {{as of|2022|lc=y}}.
Asia's population is projected to grow to 5.25 billion by 2055, or about 54% of projected world population at that time.<ref name="q072">{{cite journal | last1=Ritchie | first1=Hannah | last2=Rodés-Guirao | first2=Lucas | last3=Mathieu | first3=Edouard | last4=Gerber | first4=Marcel | last5=Ortiz-Ospina | first5=Esteban | last6=Hasell | first6=Joe | last7=Roser | first7=Max | title=Population Growth | journal=Our World in Data | date=2023-07-11 | url=https://ourworldindata.org/population-growth#explore-data-on-population-growth | access-date=2025-12-29 | page=}}</ref> [[Population growth]] in Asia was close to 0.55% p.a. {{as of|2022|lc=y}}, with highly disparate rates. Many [[Western Asia]]n and [[South Asia]]n countries have growth rates far above the world average, notably [[Pakistan]] at 2% p.a., and [[India]] with a 0.6% increase in 2022. On the other hand, [[East Asia]]n nations are in the middle of a demographic stagnation, with [[China]] experiencing a small decrease of –0.06%, after years of rapidly slowing growth.

==Socioeconomics==
{{further|Economy of Asia}}
[[File:Asian countries by HDI (2019).svg|thumb|A choropleth map showing Asian countries by Human Development Index, based on 2019 data from the [http://hdr.undp.org/sites/default/files/hdr2020.pdf 2020 Human Development Report]. {{legend|#003C00|≥ 0.900}}

Asia is home to some of the world's largest economies, including China, India, Japan, South Korea, Indonesia, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia, several of which are members of the [[G-20 major economies|G20]] and [[BRICS]]. Economic and social development varies significantly across the continent.<ref>{{cite web |title=IMF raises Asia-Pacific growth outlook to 4.5% for CY24 |url=https://www.livemint.com/economy/imf-raises-asia-pacific-outlook-to-4-5-for-cy24-11714470792559.html |publisher=Mint |date=2024-04-30 |quote=China is the largest economy in the region and India the third-largest, coming in after Japan.}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=G20 Presidency |url=https://www.gov.za/news/events/government-activities/g20-presidency |publisher=Government of South Africa |access-date=2025-08-29 |quote=The G20 comprises 19 countries including: ... China, India, Indonesia, Italy, Japan, Republic of Korea, ... Saudi Arabia, ... Türkiye ...}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=BRICS grows, adding 13 new 'partner countries' at historic Summit in Kazan, Russia |url=https://en.interaffairs.ru/article/brics-grows-adding-13-new-partner-countries-at-historic-summit-in-kazan-russia/ |publisher=International Affairs |date=2024-10-31 |quote=As of October 2024, BRICS has nine members... 5 original members: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa. 4 new members... Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, United Arab Emirates.}}</ref>

The [[Human Development Index]] (HDI) provides a broad measure of socioeconomic well-being, combining income, life expectancy, and education. Across Asia, HDI scores range from very high in countries such as Hong Kong, Singapore, and South Korea, to lower levels in parts of South and Southeast Asia. The table below shows the 10 highest and lowest HDI scores in the region.<ref>{{cite web |title=Human Development Report 2023-24 |url=https://hdr.undp.org/content/human-development-report-2023-24 |publisher=United Nations Development Programme |access-date=2025-08-29}}</ref>
